local_verdict_reason: Correctness PASS (parent-preexisting wide-FP32 golden mismatch only). Both primary probe shapes (1x32768, 1x16384 FP32) have parent and candidate same-binary PASS and show stable performance regression: +23.89% and +21.17% paired median, 6/0 favoring parent on both. 8x8192 clean pairs also favor parent +10..18%. This is a clear, consistent degradation, not noise. N1 hypothesis refuted.
root_cause_hypothesis: Zero-barrier chunked Adds were correctness-safe but not faster: replacing each 4096-element ReduceSum with 32 small Add dispatches (and the collapse with one ReduceSum(128)) multiplies vector-instruction dispatch count (D/128 Adds per row vs tileCount+1 ReduceSum calls). The per-call overhead of many small Adds exceeds any V/S saving from removing the ReduceSum API calls. Consistent with V002's lesson in a different form: it is not the barrier chain (V004 had zero barriers) and not the summation order — the manual reduction instruction count is the cost. ReduceSum as an API call is cheaper than an equivalent hand-decomposed Add sequence on this toolchain.
architecture_conclusion: FOURTH large-D reduction-topology variant refuted (V001 fold, V002 tree, V003 short-span, V004 binned single-stage). Reduction topology on frozen R31B-V011 has no remaining win: both structural extremes (fewer ReduceSum calls via manual Adds; shorter spans via pre-fold) lose or stay neutral. The per-tile ReduceSum API call is already near-optimal for this shape band. Reduction V/S is confirmed NOT the large-D bottleneck.
